baslik: The Cancer Machine That Trusted Its Own Software

basliklar: The Cancer Machine That Trusted Its Own Software
Why the Therac-25 Overdosed Its Patients
The Race Condition That Burned Patients
sahneler: A cancer machine's own software overdosed its patients.
It released up to two hundred fifty times the normal dose.
It was the Therac-25, a computer-controlled radiation therapy machine.
Earlier models had hardware interlocks to stop such faults.
This one removed them and relied on software checks.
Concurrent programming errors, called race conditions, slipped past those checks.
At least six accidents followed.
Now safety-critical machines keep independent hardware protection.

kanit.iddia: It was a computer-controlled radiation therapy machine.

Previous models had hardware interlocks to prevent such faults, but this one removed them and depended on software checks for safety.
It was involved in at least six accidents in which patients were given massive overdoses of radiation.

baslik: A Silent Alarm Blacked Out 55 Million People

tetik: a software bug that silenced the alarm system in a control room
mekanizma: power lines sagging into trees while a frozen alarm system hid the failures from operators, so the outage cascaded

The Bug That Hid a Blackout
sahneler: A silent alarm let a blackout spread across North America.
The outage cascaded until about fifty five million people lost power.
It began in Ohio, in a utility's control room.
A software bug stalled the alarm system there.
Operators never learned that lines were failing.
Overloaded power lines had sagged into overgrown trees.
Each failure pushed more load onto the next line.
Afterwards, grid reliability standards became mandatory.

kanit.iddia: The outage affected an estimated 55 million people.

Suddenly the tank went critical, starting a nuclear chain reaction.
It happened at a fuel processing plant in Tokaimura, Japan.

Two of them died.
There was no alarm: regulators believed criticality couldn't happen there.

sahneler: A ferry left port with its bow doors wide open.

kanit.iddia: The ferry capsized moments after leaving the Belgian port of Zeebrugge, killing 193 passengers and crew.
